$comment: SLOP-28 (EXP-1259 D4/D5): THE search list x4, ONE component for every place that searches a list and picks from it: the `#` issue typeahead in every editor and composer, the composer '+' menu's Implement issue and Run action submenus (composer-menu.json), the issue Picker and the global issue search (web Cmd+K dialog, the IDE search, the phones' search tab). Low-level, so it is also the eUI catalog's `SearchList` (packages/exponential-ui, conformance + 4 renderers). Anatomy: an INPUT row (`input.height`, the nav-search glyph, the field, trailing the muted result COUNT once a query is typed) over the hairline, then the ROWS = the Picker rows (no new row type; issue rows = status glyph, mono identifier, title; action rows = icon + name), `row.height` px on a pointer, `row.heightPhone` on phones, the list scrolls with at most `maxVisibleRows` visible and a `fadeHeight` px bottom fade while more rows sit below; the top row is preselected, Up/Down move (no animation), Enter or Tab pick, a hover selects. Results = `useIssueSearchResults` (lib/issue-search.ts: local rank + the server splice) at the DEFAULT limit (ISSUE_SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT): the editors' old 6/8 typeahead caps are gone. THE `#` TYPEAHEAD: typing `#` at the start of the text or after whitespace or `(` opens the list anchored at the caret (pointer: a popover `popoverWidth` wide; phones: a bottom sheet over the keyboard) with ITS input focused and prefilled with the token typed after the `#` (`typeaheadPrefill`), spaces allowed in the input; a pick replaces `#token` in the editor with `#IDENT ` and returns focus to the editor after it; Escape closes and returns focus leaving the editor text as typed; Backspace in an EMPTY input closes the list and deletes the `#` (deleting `#` closes it). The issue picker and the global search use the same component with their own input placeholder (ISSUE_SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER). Review #5 (2026-10-12): a `#` at the START of a line (in markdown editors AND the composer) opens the search only once a token character follows it (`#E` opens with `E`), so `# Title` and `## H` stay headings; anywhere else `#` opens it at once. The token is `[A-Za-z0-9-]*` only (punctuation ends it). Backspace in the EMPTY input deletes the `#` and the query typed so far (`1 + query.length` from the recorded start); a pick replaces exactly `[start, start + 1 + query.length)` as recorded when the list opened, never text after the caret. TEAM SCOPE (#EXP-1382, owner 2026-10-24): #EXP-2027 / #EXP-2109 (no active team): the global issue search searches EVERY member team ×4: the local rank reads all their issues, the server splice covers them. Its empty-query hint says so: ISSUE_SEARCH_EMPTY_HINT `Search issues across all your boards.` (drift-gated, issue-search-surfaces.test.ts). TYPING never waits on the rank: the input paints every keystroke at once; the rank runs off the UI thread (web: a deferred value; iOS: a debounced task off the main actor whose results are state, never computed in a view body; Android: a flow on Dispatchers.Default) over rows whose timestamps are parsed once per row (cached across keystrokes), never per keystroke. CHATS (#EDE-99, the chat store's S5; Danny's drafts 2026-11-18): the GLOBAL search only (web Cmd+K dialog in both layouts, the IDE search sheet, the eDE start menu, the phones' search tab; never the `#` typeahead, the issue Picker or the composer menus) gets a CHATS section AFTER the issues, read from the chat store's local index (chat-store.json `search.allCases`, `searchAll`) on the client itself: no server request, no device asked. SECTIONS (`globalSections`, `sectionCases`): a blank query or NO store on this client (eDE without one wired, a browser without OPFS) = today's list exactly (no section headers, count = issue rows). Otherwise the list is genUI Sections with headers: `issues` (title `copy.issues`, count = issue rows) then `chats` (title `copy.chats`, count = chat rows), each only while it has rows; Chats shows the Section `loading` spinner while the store answers a newer query and keeps the PREVIOUS query's rows until the answer replaces them (a first answer appends the section, never a skeleton); the input's trailing count = issue rows + chat rows; the empty state (`copy.noResults`) shows only when both are done with no rows. Up/Down move across both sections (headers are not rows), the top row is preselected and a hover selects; the selected row keeps its key while answers arrive, else the top row. THE QUERY = find-in-chat.json's (`findInChatQuery`: ASCII whitespace collapsed, trimmed, its first queryMaxChars code points), asked `debounceMs` after the last keystroke, OFF the UI thread (web: the store's worker; desktop + eDE: a background task; iOS: a detached task, never the main actor; Android: Dispatchers.IO), a newer query drops the older answer; `searchAll(query, hitsMax)` (the store's clamp). ROWS (`globalChatRows`, `rowCases`): the store's order (newest chat first); a chat whose root is not a synced root of a member team (deleted, not visible to me) is dropped, then at most `chatsMax` rows. A row = the existing Row ×4 (`row.chatHeight` pointer, `row.chatHeightPhone` phones): leading icon by concept (`icons.agent` for a root with an agent (an agent's conversation, the Assistant), else `icons.chat`), title = the chat list's title of that root (sessionTitle; a sealed title that does not open falls back like the list, sealed-content.json), subtitle = the hit's snippet (the store's, `…` where cut) led by `copy.you` for a person's input (kind `user_message`, or a `message` authored by a user), never for a SYSTEM input (#FEED-300: a hit the store marks `system`, chat-store.json SYSTEM INPUTS: a schedule tick, an event firing, a tagged device line, another session's message or report, a teammate's line in a group chat; those read as their snippet alone), one line, its matches painted by the genUI `highlight` bound to the query (text-highlight.json: every match, no current), trailing = the hit's date as chats.json `chatTimeLabel` (muted). SEALED, NOT OPENED HERE: the store keeps a sealed message without its body until its tree key arrives, so it is never a hit (no row, no locked row, nothing leaks); once the key arrives the body is indexed and the chat is found. A hit's chat whose title is sealed shows the list's fallback title. A PICK (`globalChatPick`, `pickCases`): closes the search and opens the hit's SESSION (the root, or the child it was said in, as the chat screen opens a child) with find in chat OPEN on the query (find-in-chat.json: the bar shows the query, its searches run as usual) and its START = the stop of the hit (`target`: an event = `e:<sessionId>:<seq>`, a tool output = that key with `output`, a synced message = `m:<messageId>`) instead of the newest; `globalChatStart` (`startCases`) = the first stop with that key and output, else the newest stop, none while no stops. The target is re-resolved as answers arrive until it is found or the store's answer is in (then it falls back to the newest stop), and is dropped at the first step or edit; landing = `findInChatLand` (an older stop pages its row in and rings it). SUGGESTION (#NEW-133, `suggestion`): the GLOBAL search only (never the `#` typeahead, the issue Picker or the composer menus). When the phrase grammar (issue-search-phrase.json: translate(text, members, now)) recognises the typed text, the list's TOP row is ONE Picker ACTION row (no new row type: icon by concept `suggestion.icon`, name = `suggestion.label` with {query} = the translated query, e.g. `Search: is:open by:lukas created:7d editor`), above the issue rows and above any section header (Issues, Chats). It is a row like any other: as the top row it is preselected, Up/Down and a hover move over it, Enter or Tab pick it. A PICK replaces the field's text with the query: the focus stays in the field, the search re-runs, nothing navigates and the search stays open; the picked query carries filter tokens, so the grammar answers null for it and the row is gone. The row is NOT counted (the input's trailing count and the section counts stay the result rows) and while it shows the empty state (no results) is not drawn. members = the searched teams' synced users (name, email: the rows that feed the creator names), now = the clock. `suggestion.cases`: {name, text, now (ISO, UTC), members, expected: {query, label} | null}, replayed x4 (`searchSuggestion`).
